newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Social Security proposal interesting.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Social Security proposal interesting.

text.p: President Clinton said a proposal to invest a small part of the social security fund in the stock market was "quite interesting" and said he had solicited a lot of opinions on the idea.

In an interview published in the Washington Post on the eve of his inauguration for a second term, Clinton said reform of Medicare and social security was dependent on an agreement with Congress on balancing the federal budget by 2002. The interview was conducted on Thursday.

"I've thought about it a lot," Clinton said of the proposal. "I have solicited a lot of opinions, and I've listened to people, even in New York, who are pro and con on it. It's quite interesting," he told the Post, adding that he did not yet have an opinion on the proposal.

Earlier this month a bipartisan advisory group recommended to the government as part of a broader report on keeping the social security fund solvent that a part of funds for old-age pensions be invested in financial markets.
